answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by splitting trust instead of multiplying it: every established member holds one vouching budget, like a single rope on a wharf that can be divided among newcomers but never duplicated. A violet newcomer vouched with a thin slice stays rate-limited until real work thickens that slice, and a velvet-tongued swarm splitting one budget a thousand ways receives a thousand slivers of nothing. Fakes stay poor because trust is conserved, while honest agents keep compounding theirs.
